entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 15093 of 2024
Applicant :- Istak Ali

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Dharmendra Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This application has been filed for quashing the summoning order dated 16.09.2023 as well as
entire criminal proceeding of complaint case no.368 of 2023 (Gudiya vs. Istak Ali and others),
pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate-Ist, Farrukhabad, under Section 498A I.P.C. and 3/4
D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali Farrukhabad, District Farrukhabad.

entities.text: Gudiya vs. Istak Ali and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3.  On perusal of the record, the Court finds that the allegations made in the complaint disclose commission of a cognizable offence and those allegations have found support in the statements recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. on the basis whereof the summoning order has been passed against the applicant.
Istak Ali vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50105867/
1

entities.text: Istak Ali vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. This Court in exercise of its power under section 482 Cr.P.C., is not required to assess the correctness of the allegation and the reliability of the evidence, the prayer to quash the summoning order and the consequential proceeding is rejected.

5. At this stage, the learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has so far not been arrested in the above case and the police is seeking to arrest the applicant and there may be coercive processes issued against the applicant by the court concerned, therefore, some direction may be issued to the court concerned for consideration of the bail prayer of the applicant.

6. As the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, decided on 07.10.2021), has already laid down guidelines for grant of bail, without fettering the discretion of the courts concerned and the statutory provisions governing consideration in grant of bail, no specific direction need be issued by this Court as it is expected that the court concerned will take into consideration the necessary guidelines already issued by the Apex court.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. With the aforesaid observations, the application is disposed off.

Order Date :- 12.6.2024 m.a.
